title.narrative: Transformative biodiversity conservation: Enabling Indigenous and Afro-descendent women-led actions

description.narrative: Working in Colombia and Peru’s Amazon, Andes and Coast, the project expands and mainstreams community-led, rights-based conservation approaches in national biodiversity and climate plans and priorities. This will lead to conservation strategies that enhance food and energy sovereignty and self-determined wellbeing among Indigenous and Afro-descendent Peoples (IPs/ADPs). The project draws on participatory co-creation methods to foster the leadership and leverage the roles, knowledges and worldviews of IP/ADP women in conservation actions. Community-led conservation requires systems change through gender transformative and rights-based solutions (incl. methods, financial mechanisms, policy/legal pathways) to the biodiversity and climate crises. The project prioritizes three components: learning and capacity sharing on local conservation knowledge; building a network of changemakers supporting the agency of IP/ADP women; and piloting of IP/ADP worldview-based conservation proposals.
